title: Derived category of an abelian category
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. A cochain complex $K$ of $\mathcal A$ consists of objects $K^r$, $r\in\mathbf Z$, and differentials $d^r:K^r\to K^{r+1}$ satisfying $d^{r+1}d^r=0$; a morphism of complexes is a family of morphisms $f^r:K^r\to L^r$ commuting with the differentials. Its $r$-th cohomology object is $H^r(K)=\ker d^r/\operatorname{im}d^{r-1}$, functorial in $K$. A quasi-isomorphism is a morphism of complexes $f$ such that $H^r(f)$ is an isomorphism for every $r$. The derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ is the localization $Q:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ of the category of cochain complexes at the quasi-isomorphisms (equivalently, of the homotopy category $K(\mathcal A)$ at the images of the quasi-isomorphisms), with morphism sizes taken in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Since every $H^r$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms it factors uniquely through $Q$, giving the cohomology functors $H^r:D(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal A$ with $H^r\circ Q\cong H^r$. $D(\mathcal A)$ is additive and carries the triangulated structure [def-weil-triangulated-category] induced from complexes: the shift is $(K[1])^r=K^{r+1}$ with differential $-d_K$, and a triangle of $D(\mathcal A)$ is distinguished if it is isomorphic to the image under $Q$ of the cone triangle $K\xrightarrow{f}L\xrightarrow{i}C(f)\xrightarrow{-p}K[1]$ of a morphism of complexes $f$, where $C(f)^r=L^r\oplus K^{r+1}$ with differential $\begin{pmatrix}d_L&f\\0&-d_K\end{pmatrix}$ and $i$, $p$ the inclusion and the projection. With these, $D(\mathcal A)$ is a triangulated category and $Q$ commutes with the shifts. See [Stacks Project, Section 13.11](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05RR), Definition 05RU.

split_report.summary: Compared with Stacks Section 13.11 (Definition 05RU, Lemma 05RT, Definitions 014Q and the cone in derived.tex) and with Mathlib's DerivedCategory.
